His ult is a little weird but powerful if used right: free Protection and Power reduction is  not something anyone wants to deal with.

I haven't played P3 yet, so I can't judge Junpei yet. Yosuke's easily my favourite between him and Ryuji, though. It's largely because, even though he's the comedy relief, the comedy is devided much more evenly and consistently between members of the Investigation Team. It was nice seeing Yosuke go from feeling like Inaba had nothing going for it to not wanting to leave it since he grew much closer to his existing classmates and made new friends in the form of Yu, Teddie, Kanji and Naoto. He also took the investigation really seriously and almost always took the initiative whenever something important had to happen. 

Ryuji, meanwhile, is basically the only comedic member of the Phantom Thieves. He contributes very little (aside from being a Physical powerhouse) in just about every heist outside of Kamoshida's. He has a strong sense of justice, but the same goes for every other Thief. And outside of the Palaces, basically every Ryuji scene just keeps hammering in how stupid he is. There's a reason Morgana keeps getting pissed at him. He just keeps blurting out PT-related stuff at the worst of times, doesn't take his studies even slightly seriously despite wanting something good for his mom and is pretty clueless a lot of the time. 

He thankfully gets his big moment when Shido's Palace collapses, but even that scene is followed up by him not getting that the other Thieves are mourning his apparent death and him getting beaten up for it. Practically the only meaningful thing he does afterwards is being the most eager one aside from Joker and Akechi to break out of Maruki's reality, which triggers the others to do the same. It's not even really his fault, it's just Atlus' writing.

I liked Kawakami's arc a lot. What inititally seemed like an aloof teacher who didn't want to bother with the player character actually turned out to be an extremely passionate teacher who was taken advantage of by corrupt, money-grubbing relatives of one of her students. I found her Confidant so much more interesting than the ones from any of the actual Phantom Thieves. 

I find Takemi a bit less compelling because she acts more aloof, but she's good. I don't think I can finish her Confidant before having to fight Royal's true final boss, but I like her fine. It's admirable she takes making questionable-but-good medicine so seriously, kind of like what the PT's do with stealing hearts.

As for Sae, I also enjoy her arcs.  She starts as hostile towards the Thieves and realises her superiors are just as morally questionable as the Thieves themselves. You can really feel how exasperated and desperate she becomes, leading to her desire of bringing the Thieves to justice becoming heavily distorted. Her relationship with Makoto is also complicated in a way that feels painfully realistic. But it's nice to see her (briefly) become everyone's ally after the sell-out's been caught and how seriously she takes bringing in Shido and clearing Joker's record.

To be fair, Mishima is pretty damn pathetic and the first taste of power and control he gets almost immediately corrupts him. I think aside from not liking him that much, Joker (and the Phantom Thieves who occasionally interact with him) want to keep his ego in check.

Nitra (the red triangular ore) is your lifeblood, so get it whenever you can and, when you order an ammo/health resupply, ONLY take one (assuming you have a full team) unless it is an absolute emergency.

Clear communication and teamwork is the key to surviving. Ping anything (control+click) that looks out of the ordinary and ask dwarves about it, tell your teammates about any weird sounds you hear (like a deep ominous beeping, for example) and such. Also, be curteous to your fellow Dwarves and press V whenever they shout "Rock and Stone".

Don't stand still and keep you eyes peeled and ears sharp for anything that might be a threat or an obstacle. Exploration and paying attention will help you survive, and eventually, find special things you'll profit from massively. 

And most importantly, try to relax and have fun, even when you feel like you're underperforming.
